Strong local consumer brand across China with seasonal peaks.

about: Vestaron is a Kalamazoo, Michigan agricultural technology company developing biological crop protection products made from peptides, small proteins found in nature, to control insect pests. Founded in 2007 and venture-backed, it has raised about 285 million dollars. B2B farm input brand, known to growers and agronomists only.

about: China's largest hog producer, raising tens of millions of pigs a year across Henan and other provinces and selling live hogs, piglets and feed. Pork output makes it a major agribusiness, but it is a B2B brand with limited consumer visibility.

US fresh food technology company whose AI platform helps grocers forecast demand and order produce, meat and bakery, cutting waste and increasing availability. Customers are supermarket chains in the US, including large regional and national banners. Based in San Francisco and venture-backed. B2B grocery tech with little consumer awareness.

US agricultural lender, part of the Farm Credit System, financing farms, ranches and agribusinesses in northern California and neighbouring states with loans, leases and crop insurance support. about: Vietnam's largest private industrial group and its leading steel producer, with integrated steelmaking in Hai Duong and Dung Quat, making construction steel, hot-rolled coil and pipes. It also operates in agriculture (livestock and eggs), real estate, home appliances, and mining. Customers include builders, manufacturers and consumers, and it has annual revenue of billions of dollars. Founded in 1992, it is listed on the Ho Chi Minh City Stock Exchange (ticker HPG) and led by chairman Tran Dinh Long. Hoa Phat is a well-known national brand in Vietnam through its steel, appliances and eggs.

American coffee company that popularised the single-serve K-Cup pod system, making Keurig brewing machines and selling pods for dozens of brands, including its own Green Mountain Coffee Roasters, Tully's and Newman's Own Organics, as well as licensed Dunkin' and Starbucks pods. Customers are households and offices, and money comes from machine sales and recurring pod purchases. It was acquired by JAB Holding in 2016 for about 13.9 billion dollars and in 2018 merged with Dr Pepper Snapple to form Keurig Dr Pepper. Strong consumer brand across North America.

Controlled by Dyer family interests, and some of its shares have been listed on the London Alternative Investment Market. B2B supplier with little direct consumer awareness.

The group sells to food manufacturers and retailers, and exports sugar across Europe and other regions, but its household names are mainly Daddy and Erstein.

Chinese social and live-video company, renamed Hello Group in 2021. Operates Momo, a location-based social and live-streaming app, and Tantan, a dating app, with revenue mostly from virtual gifting, paid membership and advertising, plus overseas apps. Over 100m monthly users at peak. Listed on Nasdaq (MOMO) since 2014. Strong mobile app brand in China. Monetisation relies on virtual gifts bought during live streams, which are shared with performers, and the company also invested in overseas social apps.

Agricultural food-technology company with a crop-design platform producing high-protein, better-tasting soybeans and other ingredients, such as pea and soy proteins and oils, sold to food makers and animal feed customers. Went public through a SPAC (Star Peak II) on the NYSE (BHIL) in 2021, and filed for Chapter 11 in 2025 and sold off assets. Its customers were food and feed manufacturers, and the company had hoped to differentiate with high-protein soybeans, but it struggled with cash and losses.

Indoor vertical-farming company that grew leafy greens and herbs with robotics, vision systems and its BoweryOS software, sold under the Bowery brand through Whole Foods, Walmart, Amazon Fresh and other grocers. Raised over $700m at a valuation near $2bn but shut down in late 2024. Consumer food brand with some national retail distribution while operating. The company operated large farms in New Jersey, Maryland and Georgia and had backing from investors including GV and Temasek before closure.

Icelandic land-based salmon farming project on the Westman Islands, planning large recirculating aquaculture capacity for Atlantic salmon. Aims to supply European and US seafood markets with sustainably farmed fish. Venture and infrastructure financed. Pre-revenue, B2B. The company plans to produce tens of thousands of tonnes of salmon, using geothermal and renewable energy in Iceland. A hatchery and farm are planned alongside the land-based facilities, using geothermal energy.

about: Ghana's state cocoa regulator and trader, COCOBOD, which buys beans from farmers, sets farm-gate prices, and sells to chocolate makers and traders, accounting for a key share of the country's exports. Ghana is the world's second-largest cocoa producer. State-owned, B2B and very prominent in the cocoa trade. It supervises quality control, export sales and farmer services, and supplies a large share of global cocoa to chocolate makers such as Mondelez and Nestle.

Taiwanese-run aquaculture technology firm that provides recirculating aquaculture systems and fish-farming consulting in Asia and Africa. Listed on Nasdaq (NCRA) after a 2022 IPO. B2B ag-tech. Nocera sells small recirculating fish-farming systems and consulting services, and it is a small company with revenue in the low millions. It also sells fish-farming equipment in Taiwan and has expanded into the US.

Pakistan's biggest urea fertiliser producer by output, selling Engro Zarkhez and other branded fertilisers to farmers via a dealer network, part of Engro Corporation. Capacity above two million tonnes of urea per year. Listed on the Pakistan Stock Exchange (EFERT). B2B brand with strong farmer recognition. The company sells to farmers across Pakistan's Punjab and Sindh provinces, and it is part of the Engro conglomerate led by the Dawood family.

Indian agritech startup serving farmers with seeds, fertilisers, advice, credit and market access via a network of village entrepreneurs, founded in 2012. Backed by Sequoia, Temasek and Prosus. Brand known among rural India. The company sells inputs, advisory services and buys produce, helping farmers earn higher prices and avoid middlemen. DeHaat reports serving millions of farmers. It has raised funding from marquee global investors.

Swiss agtech company making AI-driven precision spraying robots such as ARA, which spot-sprays weeds and cuts herbicide use for farmers. Venture-backed. B2B ag-tech. The robots use cameras and AI to tell crops from weeds, and sell in Europe and North America. Ecorobotix was founded in 2011 and raised a large funding round in 2025. Its founders are Swiss engineers and it markets to large farms.

B2B supplier, with growing sustainability profile.

Brazilian agricultural technology company developing the Solix robot and the Solinftec platform for sugarcane, soybean and corn farms, combining field sensors, weather stations, autonomous machines and artificial intelligence for crop decisions. The company says its platform covers a large area of farmland.

Manufacturer of the MK-V, a fully electric, driver-optional tractor for vineyards, orchards and small farms, built with autonomous capabilities and sold with a subscription software layer. about: Agricultural technology company that makes the BeeHome, a robotic AI-driven beehive that monitors and treats colonies in real time, rented to beekeepers and almond and fruit growers who need pollination. Beewise says its hives reduce colony loss, and customers include almond and avocado growers; the company has raised more than $100m and sells under a lease or service model.

Agricultural robotics company that makes the LaserWeeder, a tractor-pulled machine that uses computer vision and high-power lasers to kill weeds without herbicides, and the Autonomous Tractor Kit. Customers are vegetable and row-crop farms in North America. Venture-backed and private. B2B, with a strong profile in ag-tech news. Carbon Robotics says its LaserWeeder can eliminate thousands of weeds per second, with customers such as vegetable growers in California and Arizona.

European animal feed company supplying compound feed and nutrition advice to livestock farmers in the Netherlands, Germany, the UK, Belgium and Poland, with a sizable poultry, pig and ruminant business. Revenue around EUR 4bn. Listed on Euronext Amsterdam (FFARM). B2B agricultural brand, known by farmers. ForFarmers traces its roots to farmer cooperatives and has a long history in the Dutch feed industry; it also sells grain and runs farm supply services.

Maker of cutting tools for forestry, lawn, and garden, notably Oregon chainsaw chain and guide bars, and the ICS concrete-cutting brand. Sells to professionals and consumers worldwide, supported by distribution in dozens of countries. Founded in 1947 and PE-owned by American Securities after taking Blount private in 2015. Brand familiar to arborists and chainsaw users. Its products are sold through dealers and mass retailers.

Cresud is an Argentine agricultural and real estate company controlled by Eduardo Elsztain, that owns and farms land in Argentina, Brazil, Bolivia and Paraguay, producing grain, oilseeds, sugarcane and cattle, and trades farmland. It is the parent of IRSA, one of Argentina's largest commercial property owners with shopping centres and offices in Buenos Aires, and holds a stake in Brasilagro. Revenue comes from crop and livestock sales, land transactions and rent. Based in Buenos Aires, it is listed on Buenos Aires and Nasdaq (CRESY). Corporate brand with little consumer awareness, though IRSA malls are well known in Argentina.

Baladna is a Qatari dairy and food company, founded in 2017 by Moutaz Al Khayyat during the Gulf blockade of Qatar to make the country self-sufficient in fresh milk, and operating a large farm near Doha with tens of thousands of cows. It produces fresh milk, laban, yoghurt, cheese and juices, sold across Qatar and exported to other Gulf and regional markets, and has expanded production to Egypt and Algeria. Listed on the Qatar Stock Exchange since 2021. Strong consumer brand in Qatar, a supermarket staple with substantial local marketing.

Itafos is a phosphate fertiliser and specialty products company with operations in North America, mainly the Conda phosphate mine and plant complex in Idaho, plus the Arraias project in Brazil and the Farim development in Senegal. It sells monoammonium phosphate (MAP), superphosphoric acid and merchant-grade phosphoric acid to farmers and distributors in North America, and exports to other markets. It is headquartered in Houston and listed on the TSX Venture Exchange (IFOS). B2B commodity producer with little consumer awareness.

Biotalys is a Belgian agricultural biotechnology company, based in Ghent, that develops protein-based biocontrol products for crop protection, led by Evoca for fruit and vegetable disease control, targeting fungal diseases and insects. It was spun out of Flanders research institute VIB and sells to growers via distribution partners, with a US EPA registration for Evoca obtained in 2023. Listed on Euronext Brussels (BTLS). Customers are farmers and agri-input distributors. B2B agri-tech firm with no consumer brand.

Brazil Potash is a development-stage mining company holding the Autazes potash project in the Amazonas state of Brazil, which it aims to build as a large domestic source of potassium chloride fertiliser. Brazil imports the vast majority of the potash that its farmers use, so the project targets that import-dependent agricultural market, with customers expected to be fertiliser blenders and agribusiness groups. The company is run from Toronto with a Brazilian subsidiary and is listed on the NYSE American (GRO) following a 2024 IPO. It has no mine revenue yet and faces permitting and financing steps. B2B resources developer with no consumer profile.

Canadian cannabis marketing restrictions limit brand-building, and sponsorship use is heavily restricted. Moderate awareness among Canadian cannabis consumers, small by industry standards.

Nature's Miracle is a US agricultural technology company, based in Upland, California, that designs and sells grow lights, hydroponic equipment and controlled-environment agriculture systems, including LED grow lights, for indoor farming, vertical farming and greenhouse growers. Customers include commercial growers and hobbyists, and it sells through its own channels and online. It listed on Nasdaq (NMHI) after a SPAC merger with Lakeshore Acquisition II. Small company with limited consumer awareness.

Galan Lithium is an Australian lithium developer, based in Perth, whose main asset is the Hombre Muerto West project in Catamarca, Argentina, where it is building a brine-based lithium chloride production line using evaporation ponds and processing technology, with a staged ramp-up. Customers are battery chemical makers and offtake partners, including Chinese processors. Revenue is only starting from first production. Listed on the ASX (GLN). B2B resources company with no consumer brand profile.

Farmmi is a Chinese food company, based in Lishui, Zhejiang, that produces and sells shiitake mushrooms and other edible fungi, in dried, fresh and packaged forms, together with other agricultural products and food items such as health foods. It sells through wholesalers, retailers and online channels in China and exports to Japan, South Korea, the US and Europe. Listed on Nasdaq (FAMI), it has small revenue. B2B and consumer food brand with a modest profile, mostly in China.

GreenFirst Forest Products is a Canadian forest products company, headquartered in North Bay, Ontario, that produces softwood lumber and other wood products at sawmills in Ontario and Quebec, after acquiring Tembec-linked assets from Rayonier Advanced Materials. Customers are lumber wholesalers and home-building suppliers, mainly in North America. Revenue depends on lumber prices and is typically several hundred million dollars. Listed on the TSX Venture Exchange. B2B commodity producer with no consumer brand profile.

Sadot Group is a US agri-commodity trading and food company, based in Burleson, Texas, formerly Muscle Maker Grill, that trades soybeans, corn, wheat and other physical commodities globally and also ran a small restaurant and franchise business. The Sadot Agri-Foods division sources and supplies commodities to processors and food importers, with sizeable revenue but thin margins. Listed on Nasdaq (SDOT). B2B commodity firm, with a legacy burger restaurant brand that gives little consumer awareness.

about: Infarm was a Berlin vertical farming company that grew herbs and leafy greens in modular indoor farms placed inside supermarkets, restaurants and distribution centres across Europe, North America and the Middle East, with retail partners such as Kroger, Metro and Edeka. Consumer-facing in store, with moderate European awareness.

Phibro Animal Health is a Teaneck, New Jersey company, listed on Nasdaq (PAHC), that makes medicated feed additives, vaccines, nutritional specialties and mineral products for poultry, swine, cattle and aquaculture, plus performance products for industrial use. It sells to livestock producers and integrators worldwide, with revenue of about 1 billion dollars. Founded in 1946. B2B agricultural brand known to farm customers but not consumers.

Pivot Bio is a Berkeley and Minnetonka, Minnesota agricultural biotechnology company selling microbial nitrogen products, such as ProveN and ProveN 40, that colonise corn and wheat roots and supply nitrogen to the crop, reducing synthetic fertiliser use. Customers are farmers, with sales in the US Corn Belt. Backed by SoftBank, Temasek and others at a valuation of about 2 billion dollars in 2021. Known among US farmers through direct marketing.

Soli Organic is a Harrisonburg, Virginia indoor farming company that grows leafy greens and herbs in controlled-environment greenhouses and sells fresh produce, positioned as pesticide-free, to supermarkets and food service customers on the US East Coast. Little Leaf Farms is a Devens, Massachusetts controlled-environment agriculture company that grows baby lettuce and leafy greens in large greenhouses using rainwater and sells them in clamshell packs in supermarkets across the Northeast and beyond. eFishery is a Bandung, Indonesia aquaculture technology company, founded in 2013, whose smart feeders and marketplace help fish and shrimp farmers manage feeding, financing and sales across Indonesia and Southeast Asia. B2B agtech with strong local farmer recognition.

Farmers Edge was a Winnipeg digital agriculture company, listed on the TSX (FDGE), providing farmers with satellite imagery, in-field weather stations, field-level analytics and carbon programmes, with millions of acres under subscription across North America, Brazil and Europe. Drone and aerial data company, formerly known as AgEagle Aerial Systems, that makes the eBee fixed-wing mapping drones (from its senseFly acquisition), MicaSense multispectral sensors and Measure analytics software. Listed on NYSE American. Niche B2B brand with limited public awareness.

Cannabis marketing is heavily restricted, which limits motorsport sponsorship.

Hyderabad-based maker of shrimp feed and exporter of processed shrimp, one of India's largest in aquaculture feed, with a joint venture partner Thai Union and processing arm Avanti Frozen Foods. Customers are shrimp farmers in coastal Andhra Pradesh and Indian importers, with shrimp exports to the US, Europe and Asia. Revenue is around INR 5,000 to 5,500 crore. Listed on the NSE and BSE. B2B agricultural brand with limited public recognition.
